title: Split the internals dashboard into Astro loaders and client islands
description:
`website/src/pages/internals.astro` has grown into a single giant dashboard page instead of using Astro's strengths. It is now 1911 lines long and mixes server-side file loading, Astro markup, CSS, and multiple chunks of client-side behavior for the Trends, Model Stats, Blunder Analysis, and Golden Tests tabs.

Current problems:
- The page inlines large JSON payloads (`model-stats`, `internals-data`, `blunder-data`) into the HTML and hydrates substantial tab-specific logic in one file.
- Golden fixture discovery and parsing happen inline in the page.
- Shared helpers and constants are duplicated inside the page.
- Every dashboard section ships together even though they are conceptually separate tools.

Suggested cleanup:
1. Move server-side loading and fixture discovery into dedicated loader utilities.
2. Split each major dashboard area into its own client island or its own route if the UX still works as separate pages.
3. Keep only the minimal routing/tab shell in the top-level page.
4. Share helpers across the trends/model-stats/blunder views instead of redefining them per section.

This is the clearest case where the website is not making full use of Astro. The goal is to stop treating `/internals` as one monolithic JS dashboard embedded in a page file.
